item.title: European emissions proposal faces Middle East pushback at UN aviation agency
item.description:
By Allison Lampert

MONTREAL, Nov 20 (Reuters) - Plans to change the European Union's Emissions Trading System faced pushback at a global aviation gathering that wraps up on Friday, as Middle East countries challenged fresh efforts to curb pollution from airlines outside an existing deal.

item.title: Trump says he, Putin had very good talks on Ukraine
item.description:
WASHINGTON, Nov 20 (Reuters) - US President Donald Trump said on Friday that he and Russian leader Vladimir Putin held very good talks on Ukraine during their meeting in China, but said he didn't want to discuss security guarantees for Ukraine without a deal.

"We're having very good talks. I think there's a real good chance that we can get it done," Trump said at a White House news conference after his trip to Asia, where he met with Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping.

item.title: Saudi coalition launches 'special operation', Yemen's Houthis vow reprisals
item.description:
The Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis attacked the Red Sea port city of Hodeida and other targets in a "special operation" on Friday, as the group threatened reprisals.

The coalition said it hit smuggling and weapons-transporting operations in Hodeida while also carrying out attacks in Sanaa, Saada and Taiz governorates, marking an uptick after months of hostilities.

item.title: Houthi attacks add to worries over Trump Saudi nuclear power pact
item.description:
By Patricia Zengerle and Timothy Gardner

Nov 20 (Reuters) - Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure are adding to concerns about US President Donald Trump's proposed nuclear power pact with the kingdom, weeks before US senators are due to vote on whether to block the agreement.

Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis have intensified drone and missile strikes on Saudi airports, oil facilities and office buildings, raising questions about Riyadh's ability to secure nuclear plants that would be built under the pact.

item.title: Explosion on Iran's Qeshm Island linked to disposal of unexploded munitions, Tasnim reports
item.description:
Nov 20 (Reuters) - An explosion and smoke seen on Iran's Qeshm Island were caused by disposal of unexploded munitions, Iran's semi-official Tasnim news agency reported on Friday, citing an official, after having earlier reported a missile strike there.

(Reporting by Enas Alashray and Dubai Newsroom; Editing by Peter Graff;)

item.title: Saudi-led forces strike Yemen port as Houthis warn airlines off the kingdom
item.description:
By Yasmine Ghania and Muhammad Al Gebaly

Nov 20 (Reuters) - The Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis said it had struck the Red Sea port of Hodeidah to destroy Houthi capabilities on Friday, as the militants warned airlines to avoid Saudi airspace, pledging new air strikes within hours.

The developments, a day after the group struck the tallest skyscraper in Riyadh, signalled a worsening of a conflict that has brought a humanitarian crisis to Yemen and severe disruption to Saudi Arabia, in parallel with the US-led war against Iran.

item.title: In Yemen's Aden, divided government forces prepare for a Houthi assault
item.description:
ADEN, Nov 20 (Reuters) - As Yemen's Houthis push closer towards the temporary capital Aden against fragmented government forces, the city's inhabitants face a bleak choice: stay under fire or leave for an impoverished countryside.

Aden has had no major warfare since bitter street battles of 2015, soon after the internationally recognised government fled Houthi-run Sanaa and made the port city its base, but it is now being hit by missile and drone strikes.

item.title: Myanmar genocide judgment may bolster Gaza case against Israel
item.description:
By Anthony Deutsch and Stephanie van den Berg

THE HAGUE, Nov 20 (Reuters) - The International Court of Justice's landmark ruling that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya will strengthen South Africa's genocide case against Israel over the war in Gaza, legal experts said, establishing a precedent that genocidal intent can coexist with a military objective.

While the conflicts in Gaza and Myanmar are legally distinct, both cases before theWorld Court are based on allegations that states breached their obligations under the 1948 Genocide Convention.

item.title: Iran’s IRGC threatens infrastructure attacks beyond Middle East amid US-Israel escalation
item.description: Iranian military officials have stepped up threats to expand and deliver a more forceful response in case of renewed US-Israeli strikes.

item.title: Former French PM de Villepin launches 2027 presidential bid
item.description:
By Michel Rose and Elizabeth Pineau

PARIS, Nov 20 (Reuters) - Former French prime minister Dominique de Villepin announced on Friday that he would run for president in the 2027 election, joining an increasingly crowded field of centrist and centre-right candidates seeking to succeed Emmanuel Macron.

De Villepin, 73, who launched his own political movement last year, said he was running to heal a divided and "rotten" France, attacking what he called the "dead star" ofMacron's movementwhile rejecting both the far right and the far left.

item.title: Spanish court grants conditional bail to pro-Palestinian US media heir
item.description:
By Emma Pinedo

MADRID, Nov 20 (Reuters) - Spain's High Court has released pro-Palestinian donor and US media heir James Cox Chambers Jr. on conditional bail, while it considers an extradition request by the United States, according to a court ruling released on Friday.

The court said it had decided to release Chambers afterUS authorities acknowledgedwhat they described as substantial and unintentional errors in the Spanish translation of an FBI agent's sworn statement submitted in support of the extradition request.

item.title: Black market thrives as a result of siege on Yemen's Taiz
item.description:
In Yemen's western city of Taiz, men and children line the streets, selling rows of bottles filled with orange liquid, the only petrol available in the city besieged for weeks.

Since October, the Iran-backed Houthis have tightened their grip on Taiz, cutting it off from the interim seat of the internationally recognised government in Aden.

Although the Houthis deny preventing food and medical supplies from reaching Taiz, residents complain of shortages and skyrocketing prices, especially of fuel.
